 2 MACA 74/2019  2025:KER:59431  JUDGMENT (Dated this the 7th day of August 2025)
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.739 of 2016 on the files of the MACT, Ottappalam, is the appellant herein.
The claim was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident.

2. On 19.11.2015 at about 9.30 p.m., the appellant was riding a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KL-9/P-7616 along with a pillion rider from Nellippathi forest camp shed and when it reached Moochikkadavu, a jeep bearing registration No.KL-5/C- 1855 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner in an excessive speed, hit against the motor cycle, as a result of which the appellant as well as the pillion rider fell down and sustained injuries.
The appellant claimed an amount of Rs.3,50,000/- as compensation.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 filed separate written statements, denying the allegations on the part of the 1st respondent.
It is stated that the accident happened due to the negligence on the part of the appellant as he was riding the motor cycle in an excessive speed.
The petition before the Tribunal was tried along with O.P.(M.V.) No.737 of 2016, which was filed by the pillion rider of the motor cycle.
The main issue raised by the Tribunal was regarding the negligence on the part of the 1st respondent in driving the motor cycle.
It is stated in Ext.A3 final report filed by the Police that the 1st respondent was negligent and the accident happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the 3rd respondent driver of the jeep.
Thereafter, the Tribunal went on to calculate the compensation payable to each of the applicants.

An amount of Rs.37,500/- was awarded as compensation in respect of the appellant deducting 30% of compensation for the reason 2025:KER:59431 that the appellant was not having a valid driving license at the time of accident and therefore, there was contributory negligence.
4. The counsel for the appellant Sri.T .C.Suresh Menon submits that he has produced Annex.
A document issued by the Range Forest Officer, Agali Range dated 13.3.2020 as an additional document.
As per the said document, the Forest Range officer stated that the appellant was working on daily wages with the Forest department and he was given 461/- as daily wages.
The accident was happened to the appellant on 19.11.2015 and he resumed his duties only on 1.7.2016.
The main contention raised by the counsel for the appellant is that the tribunal has failed to take the income of the appellant as 15,000/- as claimed in the Petition.

Though there was a disability of 15% in Ext.P12, since the appellant was not examined to state nature of his physical and functional disability and that he had service of more 2025:KER:59431 than 19 years and that the disability will Rajan.K vs Manoj on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67879970/
2 not cause any harm to his job or income, the tribunal failed to award any amount under the head of loss of income on permanent disability.
5. It is an admitted fact that the appellant was not a permanent employee in the Forest department and he was working as a Forest watcher getting 461/- daily as per Annex.A.
Since he had a disability of 15%, necessarily there will be a loss of income in future.
The said aspect was not considered by the Tribunal.
No compensation was awarded under the head of loss of permanent disability.
Though the appellant claimed 15,000/- per month as his income, a daily waged person will not work for the entire 30 days in a month.

But the apex court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd [(2011) 13 SCC 236], held that the monthly income of even a coolie, who met with an accident in the year 2015, is to be taken 2025:KER:59431 as Rs.10,000/-. Hence, I fix the monthly income of the appellant as 10,000/-.

Ramachandrappa v. Manager,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant is having a functional disability of 15% and the proper multiplier to be adopted is 15, as the appellant was aged 37 years.
Thus, the loss of earning can be calculated as 10,000 x 12 x 15 x 15/100 = 2,70,000/-.
6. As discussed earlier, 30% is deducted towards contributory negligence as the appellant was not having a valid driving license.

Driving a vehicle without driving license may be an offence and can be punished with fine or otherwise., but that does not make him liable for contributory negligence and so, there should be no deduction from his compensation.
Therefore, the finding entered by the Tribunal that since the appellant was not having driving license, deduction of 30% towards contributory negligence is set aside.
7. It is seen from Annex.A that the appellant was not doing 2025:KER:59431 job for 7 months.
Since the income is fixed as 10,000/-, the appellant is entitled to compensation towards loss of earning for 7 months, which will come to 7 x 10,000 = 70,000/-.

Thus, the total compensation towards loss of earning will come to 3,40,000 (70,000+2,70,000).
8.
With respect to other heads, I find that the Tribunal awarded just and reasonable compensation.
Therefore, all other findings entered by the Tribunal stand confirmed.

In the result, the appeal is allowed in part, and the appellant is entitled to an amount of 3,40,000/-
(Rupees three lakh and forty thousand only).
The Insurance Company shall pay interest at the rate of 9% per annum for the enhanced amounts from the date of petition till realisation.
If any amounts have already been paid, the same shall be granted set off.

The claimants shall produce the details of the Bank account before the Insurance 2025:KER:59431 Company/Tribunal within one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment, and amount shall be transferred to the Bank account directly through NEFT/RTGS mode, within a period of one month thereafter.
If the Bank account is not furnished within the time stipulated, it is made clear that no interest shall run on the enhanced amount after the period specified by this Court.

Sd/-
BASANT BALAJI JUDGE dl/
